report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/mapping/inventory.py: verified docstring claims for _packages_on_disk, _orphan_bytecode, annotation_overreach, _module_targets, harvest, _stale_features; no broken claims.

handoff.purpose: Review inventory helpers for packaging, annotations, and harvest logic.

symbols.name: _packages_on_disk
symbols.note: Walks distribution roots, returns dotted package names with __init__.py.

symbols.name: _orphan_bytecode
symbols.note: Finds __pycache__ dirs with no sibling .py files.

symbols.name: _clean_annotation
symbols.note: Filters mapping to allowed string fields.

symbols.name: annotation_overreach
symbols.note: Returns list of annotation keys with disallowed fields.

symbols.name: _module_targets
symbols.note: Resolves entrypoints to known module paths.

symbols.name: harvest
symbols.note: Converts old inventory to annotations and narrative features.

symbols.name: _feature
symbols.note: Builds feature dict with status and merged annotations.

symbols.name: _stale_features
symbols.note: Detects stale packages and orphan bytecode, returns features and stats.

claims.text: Scoped to those roots on purpose: every directory in the repo with an ``__init__.py`` is not a candidate for the wheel
claims.why: The function only walks roots derived from listed package top-level names; it does not scan the whole repo.

claims.text: only one with NO sibling ``.py`` at all.
claims.why: The function skips any __pycache__ whose parent contains any .py file; only dirs with no sibling .py are reported.
The function returns a list of bad keys instead of modifying annotations.

claims.text: Silently dropping is how a person concludes the field works; naming it is how they learn the rule.
claims.why: The function names the offending keys in the returned strings.

claims.text: The build ignores these fields either way
claims.why: The build logic is in later chunks; this chunk only reports overreach.

claims.text: an annotation that could set ``status`` would hand the hand-written file's exact power back through a side door.
claims.why: The function only reports extra fields; it does not enforce the build's handling.

claims.text: ALL of them, not the first
claims.why: The function iterates all entrypoints and tokens, accumulating all matching known modules.

claims.text: the kairos-rename shim entry names five modules in one feature, and attaching its rationale to only one of them would lose the reason for the other four.
claims.why: The kairos-rename example is outside this chunk; the function does return all matches.
Every feature either becomes an annotation (when targets exist) or a narrative entry; env vars are preserved; if old is empty, returns empty structures.

claims.text: Every feature in the old document ends up in exactly one of the two: an annotation keyed to the module(s) its entrypoints name, or a verbatim narrative feature.
claims.why: The loop over areas/features always appends to either annotations (if targets) or narrative (if no targets).

The function preserves all human fields into either annotations or narrative; no field is discarded in the non-schema-2 path. For schema-2, it only copies allowed fields, but that is a separate contract.

claims.text: Already-schema-2 documents pass their blocks straight through; the harvest only has work to do the first time.
claims.why: When schema equals SCHEMA, the function copies annotations and narrative blocks directly.
The function only detects ghosts (stale packages) and gaps (unlisted packages), plus orphan bytecode; it does not guess intent.

claims.text: They stay in ``narrative_features``, where a human signed them.
claims.why: The narrative_features handling is in another chunk; this chunk only shows the start of _stale_features.

observations.what: The _packages_on_disk docstring says 'Scoped to those roots on purpose' and the code implements that by only walking roots derived from listed packages.
The harvest function returns stats with 'old_features' only incremented in the non-schema-2 path; schema-2 path sets matched/narrative but not old_features.
The _orphan_bytecode function only checks for .py sibling files; it does not check for .pyw or other source extensions.
The _module_targets function uses _TOKEN_RE to extract tokens; the regex definition is not in this chunk.
The _clean_annotation function only accepts string values, so non-string human fields are silently dropped in the schema-2 path.
